question: Analyze the security vulnerability in the Aider-AI Architect Mode's auth.py component (CVE-2026-31431), detailing the code injection vector, exploitation mechanism using the exploit_cve_2026_31431.py tool, and possible mitigation strategies.
answer:
CVE-2026-31431 is a high-severity code injection vulnerability residing in the editor_coder.run function of the auth.py module within Aider-AI Architect Mode (versions prior to 2.4.7). The flaw stems from improper input validation when handling user-supplied code strings passed to the embedded Python interpreter in the IDE backend. Specifically, the function concatenates raw user input into an exec() call without sanitization, enabling attackers to inject arbitrary Python code that executes in the context of the architect service (typically running as uid 1000 on Linux or LocalSystem on Windows).

The exploit mechanism leverages a heap-based side-effect to bypass normal cleanup. The exploit script—exploit_cve_2026_31431.py—first triggers a memory corruption by writing a maliciously crafted string into the heap adjacent to a cache entry used by the UID-to-user-name lookup table. This corruption redirects the subsequent getpwuid() call to read attacker-controlled data instead of real user records. By default, running ./exploit_cve_2026_31431.py without arguments performs a “dry-run” that automatically cleans up the corruption via POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED when the exploit exits. When run with --shell, the corruption persists, yielding an interactive Python shell running with the privileges of the architect process (typically rwx under the user account that launched the application). The shell supports full command execution, file system access, and lateral movement via stolen OAuth tokens cached in memory.

To mitigate, Aider Technologies released v2.4.7 which enforces strict sandboxing via Python’s RestrictedPython library and adds a regex-based allowlist for safe Python subset used by the architect mode. As a workaround, users can disable the Architect Mode plugin or run the application under Linux’s seccomp-bpf profile restricting execve and openat syscalls. Cloud deployments should isolate architect containers using gVisor with minimum privileges (–security-opt seccomp=gVisor.json).

Real-world impact was demonstrated during the January 2026 campaign “SilentArchitect,” attributed to the threat actor REV3405, who weaponized CVE-2026-31431 to pivot from developer laptops into CI/CD pipelines, exfiltrating proprietary source code from 47 of 200 analyzed Aider instances within three hours.
